question: If I invoke my agent with a thread_id but no checkpointer configured, will conversation history persist across calls?
reference_answer: Persisting conversation history with thread_id requires the agent to be configured with a checkpointer. When deployed on LangSmith, a checkpointer is provisioned automatically. Locally, pass one explicitly, for example create_agent(..., checkpointer=InMemorySaver()).

question: What's the default number of retries for a chat model, and which HTTP errors are excluded from automatic retry?
reference_answer: By default, models retry up to 6 times for network errors, rate limits (429), and server errors (5xx). Client errors like 401 (unauthorized) or 404 are not retried.

question: What's the difference between the content and content_blocks attributes on an AIMessage?
reference_answer: Content blocks are not a replacement for the content property, but rather a new property that can be used to access the content of a message in a standardized format.

question: If a model calls two tools in the same turn and only one of them has return_direct=True, does the agent short-circuit and skip the follow-up model call?

question: What are the four strategies the PII middleware supports for handling detected PII, and what does redact do?
reference_answer: Strategy table: redact = Replace with [REDACTED_{PII_TYPE}] (e.g. [REDACTED_EMAIL]); mask = Partially obscure (e.g., last 4 digits, ****-****-****-1234); hash = Replace with deterministic hash (e.g. a8f5f167...); block = Raise exception when detected (Error thrown).

question: By default, is MultiServerMCPClient stateful or stateless across tool invocations, and what happens on each tool call as a result?

reference_answer: Set streaming=False when initializing the chat model. If the integration doesn't support the streaming parameter, use disable_streaming=True instead, available on all chat models via the base class. langchain-event-streaming.md has no equivalent mechanism.

question: How do I stream output from sub-agents so I can tell which agent a message came from?
reference_answer: When there are multiple LLMs at any point in an agent, it's often necessary to disambiguate the source of messages as they are generated. Pass a name to each agent when creating it -- this name becomes available in metadata via the lc_agent_name key when streaming in "messages" mode. Use stream_mode=["messages","updates"] with subgraphs=True and check metadata.get("lc_agent_name") to track which agent is active.
notes: Confusable: both pages cover sub-agent streaming with a name= parameter and near-identical weather-agent/supervisor examples. Distinct: langchain-streaming.md (A) uses stream_mode=["messages","updates"] with subgraphs=True and reads metadata["lc_agent_name"]; langchain-event-streaming.md (B) uses the dedicated stream.subagents projection with .name/.cause -- no metadata inspection needed. Hand-written, verified. NOTE: reference_answer lightly condensed from the raw gold_passage excerpt during CSV->JSONL conversion -- worth a re-check.

question: How do I get a model to actually emit reasoning tokens in the first place, not just consume them once they're streaming?
reference_answer: Enable reasoning when initializing the chat model, e.g. ChatAnthropic(model_name=..., thinking={"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 5000}), then stream via agent.stream_events(..., version="v3") and iterate message.reasoning. Support varies by provider (check models.dev). langchain-event-streaming.md only covers consuming message.reasoning once it's already enabled -- it doesn't show the enabling step, just points elsewhere.
notes: Confusable alternate: langchain-event-streaming.md -- has a 'Reasoning content' section but only covers consuming message.reasoning; says 'See the reasoning guide...for model configuration details' without showing the enabling step itself. Hand-written, verified.

question: How do I stream nested/sub-agent runs and tell them apart from the main run?
reference_answer: When a create_agent call invokes another named create_agent (via a wrapping tool), the inner agent's events flow at a nested namespace. The name= you pass to create_agent identifies that inner agent in the stream. Named sub-agents surface on the dedicated stream.subagents projection, exposing the inner agent's .messages, .values, .tool_calls, .output, plus .name and .cause (the tool call that dispatched it) -- only named create_agent runs appear here, so plain subgraphs don't need filtering out.
notes: Confusable: both pages expose subgraph/subagent stream projections with .name-style attributes, so 'stream sub-agents' sounds answerable by either. Distinct: only langchain-event-streaming.md has stream.subagents (named create_agent runs, with .cause); the LangGraph counterpart only has the generic stream.subgraphs and explicitly defers subagent-specific streaming to Deep Agents docs. Hand-written, verified. CAUTION: exact filename/tier of the LangGraph confusable-alternate page was never independently confirmed in our session -- double-check before relying on it.

question: How do I filter streamed tokens so I only get output from a specific node/agent, not everything in the graph?
reference_answer: To stream tokens only from a specific graph node, use stream_mode="messages" and filter on the langgraph_node field in the streamed metadata (langgraph-streaming.md). To filter by named agent identity instead, use metadata.get("lc_agent_name") from create_agent's name= parameter (langchain-streaming.md) -- two different, both-valid mechanisms depending on what you mean by "specific node/agent."
notes: Confusable: both pages cover filtering stream_mode="messages" tokens by metadata during multi-node/multi-agent runs. Distinct: langgraph-streaming.md filters on metadata["langgraph_node"]; langchain-streaming.md filters on metadata.get("lc_agent_name") -- different field, different mechanism, agent identity vs. graph node. Both are genuinely valid readings, not a decoy. Hand-written, verified. question: How does LangChain generate tool calls under the hood — does it parse JSON out of the model's output?
reference_answer: LangChain doesn't parse tool calls out of raw JSON text anymore. Since 2023-03 (OpenAI's function calling release), LangChain uses the provider's native function-calling API for structured tool-call payloads, not manual JSON parsing.
notes: Verified, hand-written.

question: What's the main high-level way to build an agent with LangChain — chains, or something else?
reference_answer: As of v1.0.0 (2025-10-20), chains are no longer the way to build with LangChain -- all chains/agents were replaced by one agent abstraction built on LangGraph. Old chains/agents live in the separate langchain-classic package.
notes: Verified.

question: Does LangChain work directly with model APIs, or does it go through some message-list format?
reference_answer: LangChain uses a list-of-messages format, not plain strings. This dates to OpenAI's Chat Completion API (2023-01), which moved from string-in/string-out to message-list; LangChain adopted the same format then and still uses it.
notes: Verified.

question: Is LangGraph's agent abstraction something separate from LangChain, or is it part of LangChain now?
reference_answer: The agent abstraction is now part of LangChain, not LangGraph-only. It lived in LangGraph as of 2024-10, then moved into LangChain as of v1.0.0 (2025-10-20), replacing all prior chains/agents.
notes: Verified.

question: How does LangChain handle multiple message content types like reasoning or citations from different model providers?
reference_answer: Standardizing reasoning blocks, citations, and server-side tool calls across providers was introduced in v1.0.0 (2025-10-20) as a "standard message content format." The earlier 2025-04 update only standardized multimodal inputs (files/images/video), not complex output types.
notes: Verified. This item is 'incomplete coverage' rather than 'superseded' -- slightly different flavor than Q031/Q032/Q034.

question: Can I still pass a backend factory function to create_deep_agent, or does it need to be a concrete instance now?
reference_answer: No -- as of deepagents v0.7.0 (Jul 24, 2026), backend factories are fully removed, not just deprecated. Pass a concrete BackendProtocol instance instead (e.g. StoreBackend(namespace=...)), with an explicit namespace. Factory-style instantiation was only deprecated-but-functional as of v0.5.0 (Apr 7, 2026); it no longer works at all in v0.7.0.
notes: Verified against full changelog text.

question: What's the newest event-streaming API version for LangGraph, and does the older version still work?
reference_answer: The newest is version="v3" (introduced in langgraph v1.2.0, May 12 2026) -- a content-block-centric protocol with typed per-channel projections (run.messages, run.values, etc.) via stream_events()/astream_events(). The earlier version="v2" (from v1.1.0, Mar 10 2026) still works unchanged, but v3 is the newer, preferred option for new applications.
notes: Verified against full changelog text. Softer case than Q036 -- old answer isn't broken, just superseded by a newer option.
